objectClass.primaryType: anime humanoid learning companion, Hatsune Miku reference outfit
objectClass.notes: User selected reference-proportioned stylized cartoon reconstruction, with inferred hidden sides, then static user review before animation.

reasoning: Two hip-length broad spline-loft ponytails dominate lateral silhouette.
Unified head, fitted garment shell, pleated skirt, flared sleeves and long boots require different surface strategies.
Paired limbs, fingers and hairstyle layers require named contact and future pivots; animation remains pending user static acceptance.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Major body/head/hair/outfit assemblies, repeated bangs and skirt pleats, palette-specific trim/details and separate rear review.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

pose.type: relaxed frontal standing, arms diagonally down and out; slight reference asymmetry normalized for static neutral review

anatomy.note: Pixel guide overlay inspected by agent; body proportions are reference estimates, not generic canon. Reference ornament tips are excluded from skull HH; rear depth inferred under user accepted stylization.

definitionOfDone: Reference-proportioned stylized Miku remains recognizable from full-body and head views: teal eyes, high-root broad long twin tails, white fitted blouse, cyan tie/trim, dark flared sleeves, pleated skirt and thigh boots.
Static preview renders a genuine volumetric model from frontal, ±35°, profile, rear-three-quarter and rear cameras; user must accept static appearance before animation.
No false claims of recovered back geometry, physical PBR, skin deformation or animation readiness.

featureGroups.name: Reference head/body ratio
qualityCriteria: Approx 6.3 HH figure with waist and skirt/thigh landmarks locked before surface details.
failureModes: chibi proportions or generic box anatomy

featureGroups.name: Unified anime head
qualityCriteria: Continuous face volume; original eye-line and teal iris scale; no floating facial parts.
failureModes: hollow head, disconnected eyes, overlong nose

featureGroups.name: Scalp and twin-tail system
qualityCriteria: Closed scalp coverage, embedded fringe roots, thick flattened swept twin tails with taper.
failureModes: bald scalp, noodle hair or flat billboard

featureGroups.name: Outfit and repeated detail
qualityCriteria: Fitted white front, teal collar/tie, flared dark sleeves and pleated cyan-rim skirt.
failureModes: generic shirt or pants replacing silhouette

featureGroups.name: Contact topology
qualityCriteria: Sleeves follow arm roots, earphone/hairbands contact the scalp, boot and feet join.
failureModes: floating accessories or broken limb seams

Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

Raised or recessed relief and fasteners must be geometry, instanced micro-parts, or displacement; a map alone is an approximation (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
